title: fix(cli): request scopes a session-only device grant covers
body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199693. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199693 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a device paired with only `operator.sessions.write`, as the multiplayer guide recommends for guests, can't use `openclaw gateway call` or `openclaw tui`. The CLI asks for `operator.read` and the TUI for admin, read, write and approvals, so every connect becomes a scope-upgrade request for the admin.

## User Impact

User impact: a session-only guest can list, read and create its sessions from the CLI and use the TUI within its grant. Once the TUI has stored the grant with a device token, its connections and `gateway call` file no upgrade request. Behind trusted-proxy auth the Gateway issues the TUI no device token and `gateway call` stores none, so there each connection is refused once with a scope-upgrade request and then works within the grant. #199699 removes that refusal as a Gateway opt-in.

Devices whose grant holds the general scope are unchanged, and a device that needs a real upgrade (for example `operator.read` to `operator.admin`) still files one.

In the TUI, a session-only device gets no command list or pending approvals, because those need `operator.read` and `operator.approvals`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where the client learns its grant:**
- `gateway call` projects its least-privilege scopes through the stored device grant with the existing `projectOperatorScopesForMethod`. It narrows only when the method's session-scoped alternative still authorizes the call.
- The TUI connects within a stored grant that holds `operator.sessions.*` and none of its default scopes, unless `--token` or `--password` is given.

**A device approved before it ever connected:** it has no stored grant, so its first request can exceed it. The Gateway's scope-upgrade refusal already reports `approvedScopes`, and the client uses that:
- The gateway client gains an opt-in `fitScopesToApprovedGrant` hook that reconnects once within the reported grant, which the TUI uses.
- `gateway call` retries once with the session grant.
- The TUI stores the device token it receives with the grant, so its later connections, and `gateway call` reading that stored grant, fit it. `gateway call` keeps its read-only storage mode on the retry and stores nothing.

Until a grant is stored, each connection still files that request first, because nothing tells the client its grant before it asks. Behind trusted-proxy auth nothing is stored, so that holds for every connection. The opt-in Gateway change in #199699 removes it.

**Moves:** two moves keep the touched files within the line-cap ratchet without changing behaviour:
- CLI scope selection, including the existing `sessions.create` cwd escalation retry, moves to `src/gateway/call-scopes.ts`.
- The gateway client's host-dependency defaults move to `packages/gateway-client/src/client-host-deps.ts`. `client.ts` re-exports their types, so the package API is unchanged.

**Docs:** `docs/start/multiplayer.md` and `docs/cli/tui.md` describe the guest behaviour and when the first-connect request remains.

## Evidence

- **New tests:**
  - `src/gateway/call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5. A session-only grant reads with `operator.sessions.read`; a read grant and a method without a session scope keep their request; a refused request retries with the reported grant and keeps read-only storage on both attempts (this case fails without the read-only fix); a grant that can't serve the method does not retry.
  - `packages/gateway-client/src/client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, against a real WebSocket server that refuses with a scope upgrade: reconnects once within the reported grant; pauses without the hook, or when the hook keeps the request.
  - `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, adding session-only, read, `operator.pairing` and `--token` grants.
  - Without this change, the session-only, retry, `operator.pairing` and `--token` cases fail; the keep-behaviour cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `call.test.ts` 91/91, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `client.handshake.test.ts` 22/22, `client.device-auth.test.ts` 25/25, `reconnect-policy.test.ts` 19/19, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Restack onto #199693's pairing hint:** this branch now sits on `a675d1b23b7`, which adds the `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device and keeps an explicit `--url` in it. `git range-diff 3411a94ae50..48d8e528f08 a675d1b23b7..74994fa1a99` shows this branch's two commits unchanged, and the runs below were made at `48d8e528f08`, before the restack. On `74994fa1a99`: `call.edge-auth.test.ts` 6/6, `call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5, `call.test.ts` 91/91, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, `client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, typecheck clean, line-cap ratchet OK. On `71857425b24`, the same two commits on #199693's first hint commit: `client-bootstrap.auth.test.ts` 6/6, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Live run** at `48d8e528f08` (built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves only `operator.sessions.write`. The Gateway has `narrowToDeviceGrant` off, as it is by default and as it is without #199699.

- **Upgrade from 2026.11.3, stored credentials kept:** the same loopback trusted-proxy setup, starting on the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` package for both the Gateway and the guest. The guest device is approved for only `operator.sessions.write` and stores that grant with the device token 2026.11.3 issues it. 2026.11.3 has no shipped command that leaves this grant behind a trusted proxy (its TUI gets no device token there, `gateway call` stores none, and its other commands ask for scopes the grant refuses), so the grant is written by 2026.11.3's own CLI Gateway client from its public `plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime`, asking for exactly that scope. 2026.11.3 will not dial without a credential, so that client sends a placeholder password, which trusted-proxy auth does not check (the two `auth=password` frames). Then the guest CLI moves to `48d8e528f08` with the same state directory and runs the documented update step, `openclaw doctor --fix`; then the Gateway does the same. Without the doctor step, both refuse the 2026.11.3 databases and ask for it (`Cannot load device identity ... run "openclaw doctor --fix"` on the guest, `uses schema version 27 ... requires state migration` on the Gateway); that is `main`'s migration owner, not this change.

- **Independent review:** an independent review of this change found three issues, all fixed and covered above: the TUI narrowed when `--token` was given, it narrowed non-session grants, and a newly approved device had no stored grant.
